#132046. Can GTA 6 make $2 billion in its opening weekend? One industry analyst has run the numbers, and seems to think so

Can GTA 6 make $2 billion in its opening weekend? One industry analyst has run the numbers, and seems to think so

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (539 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Eurogamer

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, we all know the story of GTA 5 making more than $1 billion in the first three days it was on sale, right?
  • It has been revealed that at least, that's according to one analyst, Joost van Dreunen, a senior data analyst and great writer/numbers diviner who wrote some predictions in his respected SuperJoost PlayList newsletter.
  • Let's review what we already know: there is a conservative estimate of 10 million pre-orders for Rockstar's latest game floating around - something buoyed by comments from Take-Two boss Strauss Zelnick - and, even by the company's lofty expectations, we know the game is tracking "well above expectations" when it comes to pre-orders.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, we all know the story of GTA 5 making more than $1 billion in the first three days it was on sale, right? At the time, Take-Two believed this to be the fastest any entertainment property had achieved the impressive milestone - music and films included. It made history, and with ease. And it looks like GTA 6 is going to do even better.

It has been revealed that at least, that's according to one analyst, Joost van Dreunen, a senior data analyst and great writer/numbers diviner who wrote some predictions in his respected SuperJoost PlayList newsletter. "My prediction: Take-Two announces opening-weekend sales above $2 billion by Monday, 23rd November," he wrote. And you know what? I reckon he's onto something.

Let's review what we already know: there is a conservative estimate of 10 million pre-orders for Rockstar's latest game floating around - something buoyed by comments from Take-Two boss Strauss Zelnick - and, even by the company's lofty expectations, we know the game is tracking "well above expectations" when it comes to pre-orders.

Sources indicate that we also know a lot of people are shelling out for the slightly more pricey Ultimate Edition (£90). So many people are opting for the more expensive version, in fact, that Take-Two revised its financial forecast up to $3.5bn for the next financial quarter, thanks to "recurrent consumer spending" (something Zelnick clarified in an investor's call is explicitly linked to the Ultimate Edition). 10 million pre-orders, at roughly $100 per copy - that's $1 billion right off the bat.

According to recent reports, "That’s two days faster than its predecessor," van Dreunen said, "and largely before anyone has even played the game." That other $1bn will come over the weekend. And then, per the analyst, the game will sell roughly another 28 million copies over the course of the first year it's on sale. "My forecast puts first-year sales at 38 million copies, only modestly ahead of GTA 5’s 35 million. The real difference may be how much revenue each player generates over the years that follow.".

Industry observers note that but it's what follows in the newsletter that intrigues me most. "At the high end, [GTA 6] may just lift the entire industry with it," wrote van Dreunen. "In the face of AI slop and shitty mobile games that exist only to extract revenue, it will offer a reprieve. At a time when the industry is increasingly focused on making games cheaper and monetising players more aggressively, Rockstar is about to demonstrate the enduring appeal of spending a fortune to make something people actually want to play.".

So, even if you're dubious about the game and Rockstar's motivations for selling as many copies as possible, the launch of GTA 6 could be something that gives the industry a much-needed jolt of life, in the face of rampant layoffs and shrinking talent pools.

It's not all sunshine and rainbows ahead for Rockstar, though: amongst the frenzy of launch activity, Rockstar has been embroiled in legal action after it was accused of union busting following the firing of over 30 employees. The case's conclusion will be determined this week, as the game goes on sale.

10 Games to Play While Everyone Else is Playing GTA6

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (2086 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dualshockers

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways

  • Players could be waiting for a few patches before getting it for themselves (rather than dealing with any potential game-breaking bugs upon release), waiting for the game to go on sale (rather than paying the $80-100 full price), waiting for it to come to PC, or they may just not be interested.
  • Industry observers note that with that in mind, these players should have something to keep them occupied while others are diving into the huge title.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

To say that Grand Theft Auto 6 is the most anticipated game of the year is a colossal understatement, with the game already pulling in billions of dollars in pre-order revenue. However, that doesn’t mean everyone is going to be playing it.

Players could be waiting for a few patches before getting it for themselves (rather than dealing with any potential game-breaking bugs upon release), waiting for the game to go on sale (rather than paying the $80-100 full price), waiting for it to come to PC, or they may just not be interested. Either way, there are all kinds of reasons that will keep someone from playing GTA6 despite it finally coming out.

Industry observers note that with that in mind, these players should have something to keep them occupied while others are diving into the huge title. They could play other games that recently came out, especially since this year has seen many incredible releases.

So while everyone else continues to carry the hype of GTA6, you can show other 2026 entries the same amount of love.

In a recent development, if you were to break open any open world game to see what lives inside, you’d find a lot of the typical elements: quest-giving NPCs, tons of exploration, a healthy amount of combat and challenge. You get that with Crimson Desert if you were to crack open its world, but you also get some of the most unique expressions an open world can take.

The game is anything but a typical open world game, with zero slog to dredge through and an unparalleled approach to such a massive world. Seriously, as massive as GTA6 is, you’re going to be spending an equal amount of time (if not a little more) in Crimson Desert’s world.

This is one of those games where you need a good amount of time to properly sit with it, wandering the world and taking its challenge like a champ. It’s not like other open world games where you can get an idea of the world based on 15 minutes of gameplay, you’re going to need closer to 15 months before you can cement your opinion.

But I’ll just spoil the opinion for you: it’s going to be so, so cool, to where you’re going to actually be upset about it being snubbed at The Game Awards.

According to recent reports, if you grew up playing the Halo games, you’d be pleased to see that Halo: Campaign Evolved is everything you loved about them and then some. Not only is it an incredibly faithful remake for newcomers, but it also adds newly introduced content for veteran fans, meaning everybody has something they can properly enjoy.

Its singleplayer focus may be irksome for many FPS fans, but if you adored the original campaign, you’re in for the time of your life.

So sure, you may have waited 13 years for GTA6, but your inner child waited forever to feel that same magic from Halo again – and once you give the remake a chance, you absolutely will feel it throughout your entire soul.

Just don’t think about the current state of Halo, it’s better to live in ignorant bliss.

Silent Hill has been on an incredible winning streak lately, and it’s not looking to be stopping anytime soon, especially with the series’ newest entry. Silent Hill: Townfall is the most recent entry in the franchise, and it’s already carrying the torch (and tone) wonderfully.

Sources indicate that taking place in St. Amelia (a fictional island town in Scotland) rather than the titular town, you play as Simon Ordell as he goes through the tragedy of what happened there. Plus, you have to sneak around and hide to avoid monsters, a slight shift away from the typical survival horror tactics that the series has featured so far.

Sources indicate that the entire game is an unforgettable experience from start to finish, with intricate and creative puzzles that will genuinely stump you and music that only amplifies your tense mood. Combine this with the incredible narrative (as standard for the franchise), deep characters (that too) and a new point of view, it’s a game that will stick with you.

If anything, if you’re a hardcore Silent Hill fan like I am, this game will just get you all the more excited for the upcoming Silent Hill Remake and future original titles.

Sources indicate that it’s natural to feel protective over children, even in video games – but here comes Pragmata, putting you in charge of the child-robot Diana. You're not ready for the emotional bond.

As you and Diana explore the abandoned lunar base taken over by hostile AI, there are all kinds of things that you both can do: hacking, running and gunning, upgrading your abilities, teaching Diana the ways of humanity, and even dancing.

I just wish we could dance along with Diana; dancing is a joy that’s meant to be shared, and it’s far more fun to jump around with others, especially if we’re dancing with our robot daughter in space.

It has been revealed that but as you’re both trying to get out of space and back to Earth together, you’re going to feel warm and fuzzy at every interaction along the way. It's also just an engrossing, action-packed, and creative adventure, from a new IP.

It has been revealed that in the past few years, we’ve seen an increase in “dark wuxia” style of games, and Phantom Blade Zero seems to be our newest release in the subgenre. It’s an action game set in a literal phantom world, and you are armed with countless types of blades to help you along your journey … oh, and you’re also killer at kung-fu.

According to recent reports, devs describe the game as “kungfupunk,” and it’s honestly the perfect description of it. It looks good, feels good, plays good – it’s a fun time all around, with the added bonus of impeccable aesthetics from an alternate, dark fantasy version of China’s Ming Dynasty. It creates an action game that sets the bar, a latest standard for games to look up to.

It walks a delicate balance between a genuine challenge and action-packed fun, and players would be happy with the entire gameplay experience.

Combined with incredible cinematography, and we have a contender for Game of the Year that’s more than well-deserved. Regardless of what players believe the Game of the Year should be, I firmly believe that this game should win, at the very least, Best Action Game and Best Art Direction.

It has been revealed that fans of the first Control game have been eagerly waiting for a sequel that’s as good as the original, and that’s exactly what we get with Control Resonant. Instead of playing as Jesse Faden, you actually play as her brother, Dylan, as he tries to save Fresh York from anomalies – but don’t worry if you were a fan, you’ll still see her.

Cool, action-packed and undeniably wild, fans of the first Control will be happy to see that the sequel kept everything they know and love, as well as adding so much more extra flavouring (and breathtaking graphics).

It’s a direct continuation, but amplifies everything to be just better than before, including the clear Stephen King inspiration. In fact, most players are going to find themselves liking this game more than the first.

In a recent development, just saying, there’s a reason that it’s a contender for Game of the Year and several other categories – and I would honestly say that it’s more than well-deserved. It’s hard to live up to such a unique hype like with Control, yet this game seems to manage the impossible.

Sources indicate that while everyone is fighting against the police in GTA6, Gears of War fans have been fighting the Locust Horde for years; in Gears of War: E-Day, we see how this all begins. And if you’ve been a veteran Gears fan, you’re going to be pleased to know that it’s as fun as always – but then again, even if you’re a newer Gears fan, you’re still going to have a great time for entirely different reasons.

By coming to Unreal Engine 5, the game ends up going through much-needed revisions in the gameplay, especially when it comes to verticality. Yet, in spite of the adjustments, it’s still a great return to form.

Some players have complained about bugs and crashes, but they’re actually fairly few and far between, and most have been patched since its release. If one were to dive into the game now, the most they’d run into is Brumak deciding that a building is incredibly fascinating and needs a solid bit of observation.

With that in mind, this is an intense, yet super fun game that players will find a ton of time for, especially if they have been staring at it in their Play Later List.

This year has been a great year for the Resident Evil IP, with a killer movie that continues to be gushed over by fans and this year’s fantastic leading title: Resident Evil Requiem. And, to be completely honest, this is my personal pick for Game of the Year.

According to recent reports, the game has you playing as two different characters: Grace Ashcroft, whose sections are the traditional horror experience that will have you genuinely terrified, and Leon Kennedy, whose sections are an action-packed power trip. Together, the two of them have to figure out the truth behind the newest virus, Elpis, and what to do about Raccoon City Syndrome.

Recent findings suggest that it’s action horror in the purest sense: a perfect balance of horror and action, yet maintaining a focus on the horror element first and foremost. It’s executed fantastically, and I don’t think I’ve ever had as much fun playing Resident Evil as I had with Requiem.

If players were to compare all the recent Resident Evil titles in the modern era (including remakes), they’d notice something special about Requiem: it takes the best of all of them, and takes the crown as the best modern entry the series has seen so far. If anything, this makes me incredibly excited for what future RE games have in store.

If you love Star Wars and XCOM, you’re going to be over the moon with Star Wars Zero Company. It’s a genuinely perfect marriage, a blend between the two that will have fans of both IPs weeping with joy.

According to recent reports, if you’ve ever wanted to feel like the commander of a clone army, that’s exactly the experience that you’ll have with this game: but you’re not limited to having clones in your party. Your squad can be whoever you want, and you can implement whichever strategies you need to in order to be victorious.

Many players might hear about these kind of real-time strategy games and imagine a top-down, board-like UI rather than anything more dynamic, but that’s not how it is in Zero Company. In fact, the game is incredibly cinematic, immersing you in ways that you normally wouldn’t be if it was any other RTS title.

Basically, if you’re looking for the game to have the ultimate nerd-out with, look no further.

Nintendo knows how to keep a loyal fanbase like with the Zelda franchise, and that grip has only gotten stronger with the recent release of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake.

Sources indicate that this remake isn’t like the 3DS ports that just improve what’s already there, no, this is a remake that’s rebuilt from the ground-up, and it’s just as incredible as we remember from our childhood. In fact, many fans (including veteran fans of the OG) would argue that it’s better than the original. Of course, there are purists, but purists will always have purist takes.

Recent findings suggest that it’s hard to recapture the magic of the original, yet somehow, the remake manages to make the game feel even more magical, but with more updated gameplay (more reminiscent of Breath of the Wild) for modern players and better graphics. Seriously, what is not to love about a classic like this one?

Personally, I do think that Zelda can (and very likely will) outperform GTA6 at The Game Awards, because while GTA6 was easily the most anticipated game of all time, Ocarina of Time was, is, and always will be the most iconic game of all time.

Where To Find The Marbelle Hotel Safe Code In GTA 6

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that there are a lot of easter eggs and references throughout Grand Theft Auto 6.
  • In a recent development, one of these is the Marbelle Hotel in Vice City, which is an unremarkable-looking building that's hiding a pretty spooky experience inside.
  • Sources indicate that if you're looking to find this easter egg, you will need to first make your way to Vice City in the center of the map.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that there are a lot of easter eggs and references throughout Grand Theft Auto 6. While some are more well-hidden than others, a few can be easily stumbled across even if you're not looking for them.

In a recent development, one of these is the Marbelle Hotel in Vice City, which is an unremarkable-looking building that's hiding a pretty spooky experience inside. Here is where to find it, how to trigger the easter egg, where the Marbella Hotel Safe code is, and if you get anything for your troubles.

Sources indicate that if you're looking to find this easter egg, you will need to first make your way to Vice City in the center of the map. Once you arrive, head to the Crosstown district and go south towards the Pawn & Gun — Crosstown store. Just east of this store, about a block away, will be the Marbelle Hotel, which is a small three-story building that has a pretty worn and old facade. The front door will be locked, so head around the back and use the unlocked door.

Sources indicate that once inside, you will see a safe on your right, but we don't have the code right now, so instead head up the stairs. When you reach the third floor, the door will open on its own (I'm sure it's fine), but don't go inside right away.

Instead, loop around the railing by the stairs to find a Ratface card on the old dresser in the corner. When you're ready, head through the door that opened and attempt to go up to the roof via the small staircase. Unsurprisingly, the door behind you will shut and lock, trapping you in this stairwell.

Recent findings suggest that A bunch of spooky symbols and drawings will then appear all over the walls around you, and a heavy fog will flood the hotel and surrounding area. After a few seconds, the doors will unlock, but your visibility will be heavily limited due to the fog. Don't panic; there are actually no enemies or monsters you need to deal with.

Once the doors open, go onto the roof of the hotel and walk forward when you exit. On the ground, there will be a notepad that will give you a lot of lore about the Marbelle Hotel, along with the safe code, which is circled near the bottom of the notepad. You can also see the code briefly when all the symbols appear on the wall!

Now, head back downstairs and go to the safe and enter the code 955214. Doing so will unlock the safe, which contains some cash along with the legendary Cash and Crowex Ambassador Breakfast watch that you can use on either Jason or Lucia.

You will now be free to leave, as there are no more secrets outside of a pipe you can use as a melee weapon, which is another reference to Silent Hill, since it's a classic weapon throughout the franchise. Additionally, this will unlock the "The Truth Is Out There" trophy, which requires you to encounter one of a few specific supernatural occurrences.

Crusader Kings publishers Paradox announce CEO swap, say they're "in a strong position at a time when much of the industry is facing major challenges"

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, paradox Interactive, publishers of umpteen strategy genre stalwarts including Crusader Kings, Europa Universalis, and Hearts of Iron, have declared looks to switch overlords early next year.
  • In a recent development, while the move's been announced this week, Lilja will properly become boss from January 4th, making this a case of getting a newly introduced figurehead in place as the calendars swap.
  • It has been revealed that "My plan was never to be CEO for life," Wester said.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, paradox Interactive, publishers of umpteen strategy genre stalwarts including Crusader Kings, Europa Universalis, and Hearts of Iron, have declared looks to switch overlords early next year. Fredrik Wester will make way for Mattias Lilja, as the deputy CEO takes the throne.

In a recent development, while the move's been announced this week, Lilja will properly become boss from January 4th, making this a case of getting a newly introduced figurehead in place as the calendars swap. Departing CEO Fredrik Wester isn't going far, at least for now, as he'll "continue focusing on the company's long-term development as a member of the board".

It has been revealed that "My plan was never to be CEO for life," Wester said. "The goal was to build the foundation before passing the baton on for the next chapter in the tech giant’s journey. Since I returned as CEO, we’ve streamlined our strategy, rebuilt our pipeline and developed our commercial offering. Mattias has had a central role in laying this foundation, and now is the right time to hand over.".

It has been revealed that "The Board wants to thank Fredrik for his visionary leadership and outstanding contributions over these years," stated chairman Håkan Sjunnesson. "As a result, Paradox is in a strong position at a time when much of the industry is facing major challenges." He added that Lilja is "more than ready to assume the role and lead Paradox towards newly introduced gaming experiences that last for decades".

Lilja himself declared that Paradox have "a unique DNA that has made us one of the greats in deep and engaging strategy and management games" and will be "stepping up the pace". "We will make further investments in our core business, push the boundaries of our game design, work even more closely with our loyal players, develop more and better tools and services that benefit both modders and players, and continue to sharpen our ways of working and our organisation, with player value in focus," he remarked.

As Wester alluded to, he previously served as Paradox CEO from 2009 to 2018, with a brief stint as executive chairman of the board sandwiched between that and his latest stint as CEO since 2021. Lilja has been deputy CEO since 2024 and chief of staff since 2021, having originally joined Paradox as a producer in 2009.

Industry observers note that the past half decade has been a very mixed bag for Paradox. Their major strategy flagships keep ticking along, albeit with the question of whether their next DLC will feel worth it hovering overhead near-permanently. Outside of that, however, the likes of Cities: Skylines 2, Vampire: The Masquerade Bloodlines 2, and cancelled Sims competitor Life By You have made for a track record heavy on questionable decisions and games which either flopped hard or failed to blow away expectations. Wester acknowledged back in 2024 that the company had "made the wrong calls in several projects, especially outside of our core".

With the likes of post-apocalyptic strategy game Afterworld currently in the works, it'll be interesting to see if Lilja's tenure can see Paradox finally start to nail not just their nerdy bread and butter, but also games that don't involve staring down at a major map.

Crimson Desert is a little over one week away from release, and developer Pearl Abyss has delivered the official, final list of specs for the game. The twist is that the specs not only include useful information for PC players, they also cover similarly relevant details for console players, who traditionally don’t get mentioned in those reveals.

The specs are decently detailed, but more surprisingly - except for a single instance - they don’t include upscaling on PC, another thing games have gotten too comfortable using, even with their lowest specs.

Recent findings suggest that on the official Crimson Desert website, developer Pearl Abyss has delivered a chunky post breaking down five different sets of PC requirements for the upcoming open-world action RPG. Each set indicates the graphics preset being used - and crucially, the resolution and framerate targets you can expect with each.

With the exception of the Minimum spec, all other presets do not appear to rely on upscaling of any kind. They do not say, however, whether ray tracing is being used with any of them, which is a feature that will throw all of those specs out of whack.

That same transparency also extends to non-PC platforms, which traditionally get few, if any, details about their own resolution and framerate targets. The console set of specs are extensive, just like PC, covering both PlayStation, and Xbox.

It’s granular enough to indicate which upscaling tech is being used, where applicable. This is relevant for owners of a PS5 Pro, a console that has access to Sony’s PSSR upscaling, alongside the standard AMD FSR tech the base console - and Xbox - use.

The developer has also revealed the base resolution for each mode across each console, and the resolution the image will be upscaled to using whichever tech is being utilised.

Industry observers note that and, if you’re one of the five people who play games on Mac, you’ll be thrilled to know that the specs also include a section for Mac devices, split between the different Mac chips. The quality preset being used with each is not clear, however.

Finally, there's a set of specs for the Rog Xbox Ally, covering both the X and S models.

Industry observers note that crimson Desert arrives March 20 on PC, PS5, and Xbox Series X/S. You can expect more coverage from us at release and beyond.

Recent findings suggest that you may have recently read that CD Projekt Red's in-development Cyberpunk 2 may be trying to revive the original game's online ambitions. But, if you don't want to wait the many years it'll likely be before the Cyberpunk 2077 sequel arrives, then I've got good news for you: Cyberpunk 2077 multiplayer mod CyberMP is now out in open beta.

"After almost six years of development, countless reworks, and code rewrites, we're finally launching the public beta," the modders on the CyberMP Discord channel wrote (thanks RPS). "Anyone can jump in and play now - no invites or applications needed." The team notes, however, that this is "true beta", meaning "Crashes, desyncs, and server drops under heavy load are completely normal for now. That's exactly why we need testers.".

Industry observers note that alongside the potential shakiness, the devs say it's also possible the mod could ping your anti-virus software, since it "doesn't have a digital signature yet". Whilst the priorities for the team lie in "polishing the foundations" and "fixing crashes and stability", more features are eventually planned. But for now, they stress, "let's see how the project handles real player traffic!".

According to recent reports, so, what exactly is it? CyberMP is a dedicated multiplayer modification for Cyberpunk 2077 that allows you and your friends to explore Night City together: drive vehicles, engage in combat, and play custom community-created game modes on high-tick dedicated servers. You need an official copy of the game to play it (obviously), and the mod is completely free to download. You can download the mod, and read a fair amount of how to get it working, what to expect from it, and how to troubleshoot any challenges, over at its dedicated website.

If you're thinking 'Hang on, why does Cyberpunk 2077 multiplayer sound so familiar?', it's because the game was supposed to receive an official multiplayer mode after its original release. Thanks to its shaky launch, however, plans changed, and CD Projekt Red later declared that multiplayer would be a separate "triple-A release", but, eventually, that too was cancelled. The studio is still keen to honour the idea, though, and recently stated it's "focusing on bringing online into all of our franchises one day".

It has been revealed that this isn't the first massive bit of news we've had about Cyberpunk 2077 mods this week. Just yesterday, a newly introduced mod called 'Torrent' added 3D rain, lightning storms, and tyre spray to Night City - all rendered and made lovely with a new lighting system that seems to play nicely with other weather mods that have been created for the game.

Recent findings suggest that what's the best prank you ever pulled on a teacher in school, assuming you went to school? By which I mean, a genuinely funny prank that didn't cause any injuries, break any of the more vital laws (legal or ethical), or leave anybody with years of mental distress.

I'll start: I once had to write a four-page punishment essay with the topic "silence is golden", after being caught talking in class. I took the essay very seriously for the first three pages, only to end it with the phrase "...but not as golden as my arse." The teacher who set me the essay smugly tore it up without reading it - as I knew he would. Checkmate, Mr Thompson. Decades later, the last laugh remains mine.

Worst Class Ever is a new don't-call-it-friendslop asymmetrical multiplayer game dedicated to such larks. One player is a teacher, and seven others are naughty delinquent children, hiding in amongst some well-brought-up and obedient NPCs. As the wayward tykes, your goal is to do mischievous things like eating at your desk, passing notes, dropping banana skins, and playing on your phone, without being spotted by Teach.

In a recent development, all of this takes place in a breezy modern Japanese high school, the kind familiar from a million animes. Bagsy the Protagonist Desk by the window at the back of the class! The maplist spans the curriculum, from computer labs to gym tracks to stepped lecture theatres. I don't think there are any covert edu-tainment mechanics, but if you're playing Teacher, I guess there's nothing to stop you actually explaining the periodic table while trying to work out who keeps throwing chalk at your head.

Recent findings suggest that what a wholesome and whimsical place! Such happy memories! Oh crikey, the male teacher is terrifying – why can't he stop grinning? And why do I have a smoke grenade? Why is this lesson taking place in the dark? Why are the teachers permitted to punch the students and tie them to wooden posts? Worst Class Ever definitely isn't a horror game, but I'm not sure I'd send my kids to this particular institution. I feel like we're one texture pack away from playing a more sociable version of Little Nightmares. Read more on Steam.

10 Google Privacy Hacks Everyone Should Know

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (955 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • From managing your Gmail inbox to downloading apps on your Android phone, pretty much every aspect of your digital life has a little bit of Google in it.
  • Your Gmail account doesn't just have one email address.
  • Sources indicate that if you wish to make your emails more private, you can also link your Proton Mail account to Gmail.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

From managing your Gmail inbox to downloading apps on your Android phone, pretty much every aspect of your digital life has a little bit of Google in it. That is a lot of power in the hands of a company that makes money by selling your data to advertisers. While you can't fully escape Google's tracking without quitting a whole bunch of essential online services, you can use these privacy hacks to reduce how the company tracks you, as well as protect the information in your Google account.

Your Gmail account doesn't just have one email address. In fact, it has unlimited addresses, but you need a hack to utilize them. When you're signing up for a fresh service, you can add another word to your email address, as well as the "+" symbol, to create an alias. For example, if your email is "[email protected]," and you're signing up for an Amazon account, you can use "[email protected]" as your email address. The email will still end up in your main inbox, as if you simply used [email protected]. Not only can this trick turn one Gmail address into an unlimited number of addresses, but it also helps you identify who sold your email address to spammers, because those emails will have the alias in the "To" field.

Sources indicate that if you wish to make your emails more private, you can also link your Proton Mail account to Gmail. This lets you send and receive emails via your Gmail address, while using Proton Mail's privacy protections such as blocking email trackers.

Google wants to show you personalized search results, which initially feels very helpful, but it also ends up trapping you in an algorithmic bubble. The best way to break out of your search bubble is to periodically use other search engines, but if you wish to stick to Google, you can disable personalized search recommendations in Google Search and the Play Store on Android. Go to this settings page, and turn off Personalized Recommendations and Play Personalization.

Google tracks your web and app activity by default, which includes your search history, voice data (if you use the speak-to-search feature), and activity from sites, apps, and devices that use Google services. However, associated information, such as your location data, is also saved to your Google profile, which you might not assume gets included in "Web & app activity." Fortunately, you can disable this tracking by going to this settings page, scrolling down to "Web & App Activity," and turning off all options in this section.

Google's Timeline feature saves your location in Google Maps to create a map of places you've visited. This is useful if you want to keep track of your recent stops; however, Google can use Timeline data to help businesses see how effective their ads were, or how likely you are to visit nearby stores. Its confirmation page confirms this: "Depending on your settings, activity saved as history in your Google Account, including ad interactions, may also be connected to Timeline data to help nearby businesses estimate the likelihood that people will visit their stores. No personal information is shared with businesses.".

Timeline isn't enabled by default, but in case you enabled it a while ago, and are no longer using it, you can turn it off by going to this settings page. Click Turn off, and delete your activity to remove Timeline data from your Google account.

Industry observers note that you can't fully escape Google's ads or tracking, but you can disable personalized ads to stop the company from using your account data to show ads. To do this, go to this settings page, and turn off Personalized ads.

While Google claims that it isn't using your emails to train AI, the company does offer AI features that make your emails feel more robotic than human. One of these is "Smart Reply," which offers email reply suggestions such as "Got it. See you soon." I can type that on my own, and I feel uncomfortable with Gmail analyzing the contents of my emails and replies to offer suggestions that I wouldn't use anyway. You can disable this by going to Gmail Settings > General, or by visiting this settings page. Scroll down to "Smart features," and turn off the checkbox next to it. This will disable Smart Compose, Smart Reply, suggestions for pending replies and follow-ups, spelling, grammar, and autocorrect.

A physical security key is a great security upgrade. It's a physical barrier that prevents most ways to hack into your account remotely. Even if someone discovers your email ID and password, and has access to your two-factor authentication code, they won't get in without physical access to that key. You can check out Google's support page for physical security keys for more information on compatibility and setting up your security keys.

If you're serious about your online privacy and security, I'd advise against keeping your primary credit card saved to your Google account. If your account is compromised or your device is stolen, you risk exposing your credit card to fraud. Instead, use a prepaid virtual card with your Google account. Sites such as Privacy.com offer single-use or merchant-locked prepaid cards, and they allow you to set spending limits too. You can use such services with your Google account to reduce the chances of losing money if your account gets hacked.

Recent findings suggest that google uses data from Gmail and Google Drive to target ads, which means that your emails, files, and photos could be used for monetization. To stop this, you'll need to disable Personal Intelligence. To turn it off, visit this settings page, and click Turn off Personal Intelligence.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that battlefield Studios has unveiled that Battlefield 6 is going free to play for one week next week.
  • Industry observers note that though it does not encompass the entirety of the game, the free trial is fairly generous.
  • For starters, the trial kicks off Tuesday, March 17 and will run until the following Tuesday, March 24.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that battlefield Studios has unveiled that Battlefield 6 is going free to play for one week next week. Well, a portion of the game is, anyway, as part of a free trial that will include some of the game’s most popular modes and maps.

Industry observers note that though it does not encompass the entirety of the game, the free trial is fairly generous. Here’s what to expect.

For starters, the trial kicks off Tuesday, March 17 and will run until the following Tuesday, March 24. The trial will be accessible from Battlefield Redsec, the already free-to-play portion of the game.

Recent findings suggest that once downloaded, you’ll find a new Battlefield 6 Free Trial section in the main menu. Because Redsec and Battlefield 6 multiplayer share progression, if you played the former at any point, you’ll be able to pick up from where you left off.

The same is also true the other way around; if this is your first time with Battlefield 6, all your unlocks will carry over to the full version, as well as to Redsec if you decide stick with the free-to-play off-shoot.

Once it kicks off, you’ll find three playlists to choose from. Casual Breakthrough, All-out Warfare, and a third playlist showcasing the newly introduced Nightfall game mode and its associated map.

Sources indicate that all-out Warfare is what you come to Battlefield for, and that playlist features Conquest, Breakthrough, as well as BF6’s newcomer Escalation - all large-scale, combined arms game modes. They will be playable across four maps. You get to play on two from Season 2: Contaminated, and Hagental Base, one from Season 1: Eastwood, and Mirak Valley from the base game.

It has been revealed that casual Breakthrough is based on a playlist that already exists in the core game, and it’s really designed as a nice on-ramp for new players. It also offers less intense gameplay, perfect for people grinding unlocks.

Sources indicate that casual Breakthrough is limited to just 16 real players (eight per team), with the rest filled up with bots. You earn the same amount of XP in those matches, except when you interact with bots, so killing a bot will net less than a human player. Outside of that, unlocks, Challenges and all other things that don’t depend on stat-tracking can be done within.

In the trial, the Casual Breakthrough playlist includes Hagental Base, Contaminated, and Eastwood.

The most interesting is the third playlist, in part because its content will also be available to owners of the full game for the first time right alongside free-to-play players. Nightfall is a playlist exclusive to the Hagental Base map.

This is a very small map, so the mode selection here is Team Deathmatch, Squad Deathmatch, and Domination. Under Nightfall conditions, lights across the entire map are turned off, so you’re going to have use your NVGs to be able to see. This is also a god opportunity to try out weapon attachments that specifically work under low-light conditions, which typically don’t get much use in multiplayer.

March 17 also marks the launch of the second stage of Battlefield 6’s Season 2, which comes with the aforementioned Nightfall content, as well as a massive fresh upgrade - so the timing works out nicely for everyone.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that with the launch of World of Warcraft: Forever there's a whole upcoming world filled with niche gear and strange baubles to collect.
  • That add-on is All the Things, a must-install for collectors like me, as it acts as a database of all the gear, mounts, titles, crafting recipes, and super rare drops in the game.
  • On occasion, specific items have written notes attached by the All the Things development team, as is true of a special World of Warcraft: Forever toy, the Pouch of Violet Dust.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that with the launch of World of Warcraft: Forever there's a whole upcoming world filled with niche gear and strange baubles to collect. But one item in particular has drawn the ire of the creators of a popular completionist add-on.

That add-on is All the Things, a must-install for collectors like me, as it acts as a database of all the gear, mounts, titles, crafting recipes, and super rare drops in the game. Once you collect something, it is hidden in the add-on, thus tracking your progress and making for a fantastic tool for picking the game apart.

On occasion, specific items have written notes attached by the All the Things development team, as is true of a special World of Warcraft: Forever toy, the Pouch of Violet Dust. This is a promotional item that was obtainable by watching two hours of WoW Forever streams between the 4th and 12th November.

Sources indicate that it's a powerful toy! When used on a campfire, it changes the fire's colour to purple and extends the buffs provided by it from the usual one hour to two hours. But the sticking point with the item isn't its existence, rather the fact that it's going to be removed in early December, not long from now.

This is what the creators of the All the Things add-on don't like. "A week-long, Twitch-only window for an item that gets taken away a month later is exactly the kind of FOMO that disheartens collectors," the creators stated in a note attached to the item in the mod. "It can't be earned by playing the game at all. Even those who get it don't get to keep it.".

Industry observers note that they aren't alone in feeling this way. Comments below the item's listing on the Wowhead database are equally scorching. "I love FOMO in their explicitly non-fomo game," wrote user TheWhiteRose.

"Just... Why?" added user Darrenic427. "They could very easily just patch out the camp buff duration and keep the visual effect, but Blizzard just doesn't like pretty fire I guess. Figures that they finally give us access to purple fire but then take it away after a month.".

Recent findings suggest that the battle between collectors and time-limited FOMO items is one that has been waged for about as long as these sorts of items have been a part of games. Though for the pouch, it's an especially weird case: an item that's cool to have but so temporary in nature that it makes it both important to completionists and strangely pointless to care about. Whether it makes a return in a later patch for World of Warcraft: Forever and doesn't require out-of-game actions to obtain, and doesn't disappear, we'll have to wait and see.

In a recent development, woW Forever itself is proving popular among players - me included. It's added a staggering amount of new quests and many new features to the original version of World of Warcraft, which, in turn, has injected the game with an impressive amount of new items to collect. Completionists will likely be glued to the game for a long time.

Industry News: Garmin Cyclists Can Now Make Themselves Appear on Waze in Real Time

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Cyclists who ride with Garmin gear can now appear as live, moving icons on the Waze driving app, and nearby drivers will receive an alert to slow down and watch for them on the road.
  • Recent findings suggest that for riders already using Garmin devices, opting in costs nothing and adds a upcoming layer of safety, particularly on roads where drivers may not expect cyclists.
  • Riders can simply opt in once through Garmin Connect.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Cyclists who ride with Garmin gear can now appear as live, moving icons on the Waze driving app, and nearby drivers will receive an alert to slow down and watch for them on the road.

Recent findings suggest that for riders already using Garmin devices, opting in costs nothing and adds a upcoming layer of safety, particularly on roads where drivers may not expect cyclists. The feature is rolling out now, but you should be aware of its limitations.

Riders can simply opt in once through Garmin Connect. After that, sharing starts automatically when an outdoor cycling activity begins and stops when the ride ends. While a ride is underway, Waze owners near the cyclist see a cyclist icon move along the road and receive a Live Cycling Alert reminding them to slow down and stay aware.

The feature runs on LiveTrack, Garmin's existing live location-sharing tool, which lets friends and family follow a rider's real-time location, speed, course, and more. Garmin claims this collaboration extends that peace of mind to motorists, giving them greater awareness of their surroundings.

Garmin notes its location sharing is temporary and session-based. The rider's name, identity, and route are hidden, and no personal information is shared or displayed in Waze. Drivers see only an anonymous icon and the alert.

You'll need a few things to get this feature up and running:.

A compatible Garmin Edge bike computer or Garmin watch.

A phone running Garmin Connect with a data connection.

An outdoor cycling activity (the feature doesn't apply to indoor rides).

The good news is using the feature is free: LiveTrack costs nothing on compatible Garmin bike computers and watches, and Waze is free for drivers.

This new feature is a great safety perk, but there are real-world caveats worth considering:.

It has been revealed that this feature is for Waze only. Alerts reach drivers only when Waze is open on their phone. Google Maps, which has far more users, is excluded, so a large portion of the drivers you share the road with won't see you this way.

Recent findings suggest that it depends on your phone's signal. Your position travels from the Garmin to your phone, then to Garmin's servers, then to Waze, and finally to the driver's phone. On a patchy rural signal, a few seconds of lag could put the icon on the wrong side of a bend from where you actually are. A rider who leaves their phone at home or whose phone loses signal simply won't show up on a Waze map, as a ride without a data connection is invisible to Waze.

Industry observers note that finally, remember to treat this safety feature as an extra perk, not a guarantee. At the end of the day, it isn't a replacement for bike lights, bright clothing, and defensive riding.

#132030. Exclusive – Behind The Romance: Rockstar Talks GTAVI’s Jason And Lucia

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1576 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Gameinformer ↗ Open Full Page

Exclusive – Behind The Romance: Rockstar Talks GTAVI’s Jason And Lucia

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1576 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gameinformer

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that after dozens of hours exploring Leonida, I have a lot of positive things to say about Grand Theft Auto VI, and shared as much in our review of the game.
  • We reached out to senior members of the Rockstar Games team to ask about their thoughts on Jason and Lucia, and this is what they had to share.
  • It has been revealed that during my playthrough, the Jason and Lucia dynamic really elevated the experience, adding heart and emotional weight to the expected mix of action, driving, and activities around Leonida.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that after dozens of hours exploring Leonida, I have a lot of positive things to say about Grand Theft Auto VI, and shared as much in our review of the game. But for my part, the feature that elevated the game most prominently above Rockstar Games’ other (excellent) games wasn’t its graphics, missions, or action – it was the storytelling and interplay between the two lead protagonists. Jason and Lucia bring heart, emotional depth, and a sense of genuine threat to the crime fantasy, as you grow attached to them and start cheering for them against all the odds stacked against them.

We reached out to senior members of the Rockstar Games team to ask about their thoughts on Jason and Lucia, and this is what they had to share.

It has been revealed that during my playthrough, the Jason and Lucia dynamic really elevated the experience, adding heart and emotional weight to the expected mix of action, driving, and activities around Leonida. Was a couple or romantic relationship the plan or goal for the game from very early on in development, or did that come later? Do you see the focus on Jason and Lucia’s relationship as one of the features that separates Grand Theft Auto VI from your prior work on storytelling in the game series?

Recent findings suggest that stephen Donkin, Vice President of Design: “The dual protagonists and the relationship between the two of them was there from very early in development, but exactly how that was expressed in the game did change over time. It was an enormous challenge for us to get them working together in the open world together and finding exactly how that would work. As we started to layer in more mechanics, dialogue, and incremental features across all teams, it just clicked at some point. The ability to be together in the open world also allowed us for newly introduced ways to tell the story of the game and to bring some of the exposition and narrative into the open world in a way we hadn’t been able to do before. Hearing these little bits of dialogue as you are just tooling around the world that have specific context to what you as a player have just been doing in the story really knits it all together.”.

The player has a choice for how to develop the relationship between the two leads, but I imagine most players are drawn toward helping it thrive. In early playtests, is that what you observed?

Katie Pica, Design Director: Player Systems & Progression:“Overall, we’ve seen that players are invested in supporting Jason and Lucia’s relationship but we don’t favor a specific path through the game, it is completely down to player choice.”.

It feels like a lot of the game’s driving narrative beats factor for a close connection between Jason and Lucia. Was it challenging to craft variations that included a more tense or distant connection between the two? Is that even possible?

Luke Howard, Senior Design Director: Missions & Visualization:“One of the core goals of this game was to tell the story of Jason and Lucia with a base line relationship where they are amicable, if just platonic, as they still share the same ultimate goals and need each other to achieve them. So, this gave us a good platform on the main flow to expand particularly intense or emotional moments they experience with variation that can expand on their romantic relationship, while not losing anything if that doesn’t exist. In short, we did develop variation in scenes and interactions that range from subtle to more significant, but done in a way that should feel authentic to the player’s choices, relationship-wise and also criminal profile.

In a recent development, one example is after Lucia helps Kordell’s gang pull off an intense armored truck robbery she shares the information with Raul’s crew. Afterwards Jason pulls Lucia aside to see how she's coping. This moment carries several variations where the performance direction was captured multiple ways to cover a range emotional energy between them. The actors deliveries are brilliant and nuanced – these small tender moments are where we tried to craft pieces that when added up together over the course of the story, author an authentic version of the player’s Jason and Lucia.”.

Were there any fictional couples or real-life couples that the team looked at for inspiration in shaping the Jason and Lucia dynamic, whether those couples came from substantial crime stories or not?

Rupert Humphries, Senior Vice President of Narrative:“We definitely started by looking at all the “couple on the run” movies. There are a lot of them but the ones that we kept coming back to were Warren Beatty and Faye Dunaway in Bonnie and Clyde, McQueen and MacGraw in The Getaway (the Jim Thomson book is also great), True Romance, Thelma and Louise. Clooney and JLo’s dynamic in Out of Sight, as well. And then a lot of buddy movies actually – Riggs and Murtaugh, Butch and Sundance, Mike Lowry and Marcus Burnett, etc. for their back and forth together. In terms of having a game where the characters can change based on how you play and whether you really lean into and enjoy the crime spree we thought about how both Pulp Fiction and Natural Born Killers start with a couple in a diner pulling out guns, but then how different those couples are and how different those scenarios play out. Jason and Lucia are a lot tougher than Tim Roth and Amanda Plummer but we liked the idea of telling a story where Jason and Lucia could end up being closer to either end of that spectrum based on what the player was doing.”.

Sex and intimacy are notoriously complicated and challenging to present in games. How did you aim to strike a balance with their private moments together that felt authentic? Any thoughts about how or why it’s so challenging to present adult relationships in video games?

It has been revealed that rupert Humphries, Senior Vice President of Narrative:“This is definitely something we thought a lot about and spent a long time trying to get right. The actors who play Jason and Lucia were so good, and they had a natural chemistry and part of it was just trying to capture some of that.

Recent findings suggest that there’s this trade off in making games between player control and then scripted scenarios. We try and give the player as much control as we can because we are working in an interactive medium and actually doing something rather than watching it is going to feel more powerful. But then you have the ability to really mess around and break the illusion of a tender or romantic moment or whatever it is. So the relationship aspect of this story is there if a player wants to engage in it, but if they don’t the story can play out differently.”.

In a recent development, in its best moments of genuine support, regular connection, open communication, and flirty or engagement with one another, Jason and Lucia can come across as a pretty ideal model of good relationships – even while they’re simultaneously committing major crimes together. Was that juxtaposition of a healthy romantic relationship against an external world of illicit activity an explicit goal for how the narrative came together?

Rupert Humphries, Senior Vice President of Narrative:“That was the goal, yes. You are really living with these characters – they’re eating, sleeping, showering, throwing away their trash, or not. The relationship needed to feel real to sit alongside all of that. Then even just as a development team, we live with these characters for years and years. We wanted them to be people we could like, care about, and root for. And they needed to like each other. But then the world itself is so crazy and chaotic and seemingly on the brink of collapse.

Sources indicate that when we set out to make this game, and go into that multiyear development marathon, we said we wanted to spend our time working on something with heart, and with some characters you could care about and root for. It’s barely worth even stating, but we are living in a time when people are divided along almost every line, and feelings about the future are pretty bleak. We wanted to create a world that held up a mirror to that, demonstrated that fever pitch of craziness that we are all maybe a couple of bad decisions away from, but we wanted the story we were going to tell to have something positive at its core and the message that human connection is better than division.”.

The game automatically moves you to play one character or another at certain points, but for many sequences, you can choose your playable lead. In your experience playing and watching others play, do most players gravitate toward one character or another as “their character?”.

It has been revealed that stephen Donkin, Vice President of Design:“It really varied in our playthroughs. They are both such great characters and performances that people seemed to gravitate to both of them in different ways. But overall, we have found the split of time between characters to be relatively even on a per-playthrough and also at a macro level.”.

Industry News: While soulslikes went bigger than big, Death's Door swung open the appeal of a tighter adventure

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that declaring a Best Way of Doing Things is a fool’s game, though in recent years my favourite entries in the Tricky Hitting genre – inclusive of soulslikes and their hybridised disciples – have been the major, bulging ones.
  • Industry observers note that even in the latter stages, with a full kit of precisely four ranged spells, Death’s Door is a simple proposition.
  • Still, it’s clever with its limitations.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that declaring a Best Way of Doing Things is a fool’s game, though in recent years my favourite entries in the Tricky Hitting genre – inclusive of soulslikes and their hybridised disciples – have been the major, bulging ones. Elden Rings and Silksongs, with vast kingdoms and deep, rattling toolkits for surviving them. The reason it’s a fool’s game is because you can also have something like Death’s Door, a taut, compact, lighthearted little actioner that fills eight hours instead of 80 and yet never feels underwhelming or compromised for it.

Industry observers note that even in the latter stages, with a full kit of precisely four ranged spells, Death’s Door is a simple proposition. You are a crow. You hit things. Occasionally you shoot things. You collect the souls of a frog, a yeti, and a grandmother. Everything in-between directly relates to finding the errant monster/pensioner, or at a stretch, upgrading one of those four abilities.

Still, it’s clever with its limitations. Environments are small in number but vary wildly in tone and texture, and they tightly weave their paths into criss-crossing bundles that maximise travel – evoking the sense of a great, ranging adventure within relatively tiny spaces. The lack of a wiki’s worth of combat options also never becomes a problem, partly because it spreads out its spell unlocks, and partly because the smooth, flowing back-and-forths of its central swordplay are pleasurable enough to carry it anyway. Good bosses, too! They’re all characterful, memorable weirdoes who fight unlike anyone in their minion armies, and usually come with a hidden weakness to deduce and exploit.

Recent findings suggest that which is welcome, as these major lads and lasses do tend to launch difficulty spikes right up your feathered backside, and do so in a game that isn’t otherwise as fussed about trial-and-error pain endurance as some of its inspirations. They don’t, however, bring the mood down. At times, this tale of a pitch-black soul reaper working as an agent of Death (complete with an office of Death and embittered co-workers of Death) can get downright cosy, leading through you through warmly-lit jungles and breezy waterside ruins.

Industry observers note that recently replaying, I’d also forgotten how witty it can be. Little gaglets are sprinkled throughout, both visual and verbal, but the best jokes are saved for – funnily enough – the bosses, who’ll raise your pre-fight spirit with some amusingly terrible trash talk before becoming the punchline themselves. I audibly wheezed the first time a death animation immediately cut to the foe’s impromptu funeral, their beaked killer among the precious few guests. And even when the joke is recycled later, I couldn’t help tittering at the sight of my enemy – who seconds earlier, had been attempting to fatally sit on me – lying nobly in state.

I previously considered ending my Valor Mortis review by calling it a gateway into the more demanding side of action-RPGs; a shorter, simpler alternative to FromSoft’s overwhelming titans that might nonetheless serve to introduce curious newcomers to their shared quirks and qualities. The game equivalent of splashing your chest with water before jumping into a pool. In hindsight, Death’s Door was always a better fit for that description, though there’s enough else here you don’t need to be prepping for something tougher to appreciate its lean, keen adventuring.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Leader of the UK Conservative Party (and former Mortal Kombat player) Kemi Badenoch is more worried about the amount of time people will spend playing GTA 6 rather than the game itself.

According to recent reports, every fresh Grand Theft Auto game invites some amount of controversy over its in-game violence or depictions of sex and drugs - from San Andreas' raunchy Hot Coffee mini-game to GTA 5's graphic torture scene. Ahead of GTA 6's release this week, the Tory leader downplayed those fears.

In a recent development, "I would be more worried about the amount of time people were spending on a game than the game specifically. I remember in my childhood playing Mortal Kombat and Street Fighter. I didn't hit anybody after playing those games," Badenoch said in a news conference shared by Sky News (good spot, IGN).

While Badenoch's stance might be surprising for the normally right-wing UK political party, she did still worry over children who might play GTA 6 for too long. There are probably far worse ways for kids to spend their time than engaging with a long-form story like GTA 6's, though, especially in an era with endless amounts of 10-second clips to mindlessly scroll past and declining funding into youth programs.

"I haven't played Grand Theft Auto, I know people are worried about the game content. At the same time, I'd be more worried about a kid who played it all day, who was in their bedroom all day, than one who spends half an hour on it and then went out and did something else. They are two different things," Badenoch added.

GTA 6's release is imminent and is expected to be the biggest entertainment launch of all time. One analyst even suggested GTA 6 could make over $2bn in its opening weekend - that's handily more money than Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey made during its entire run in cinemas, for context.

Why Do I Want To Paint The Walls In Grand Theft Auto VI?

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (538 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gameinformer

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that I admire the cozy sim genre.
  • Sources indicate that grand Theft Auto VI is not a cozy game, but it has a substantial amount of cozy elements and mechanics.
  • And for some reason, I couldn’t start that process fast enough.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that I admire the cozy sim genre. Stardew Valley and Animal Crossing are on regular rotation in my home on my family’s screens, but not my own. In an odd way, I find the genre stressful, arguably the opposite of its intended purpose. I will happily and cathartically guide Grace Ashcroft through the tense hallways of Rhodes Hill in Resident Evil Requiem, but Pokémon Pokopia’s seemingly endless list of to-dos makes me sweat. It’s just not my genre, and I have come to terms with that.

Sources indicate that grand Theft Auto VI is not a cozy game, but it has a substantial amount of cozy elements and mechanics. Bird (and animal) watching, for example, is apparent and encouraged early in the experience. You can also fix up your somewhat dilapidated home from almost the moment you are let loose outside of the opening tutorial missions.

And for some reason, I couldn’t start that process fast enough.

I climbed to the roof to fix the leak and replaced all the stairs leading up to the home before I ever participated in the game’s namesake and stole a car. Normally, it’s the kind of interaction I skip or choose not to engage with, given the option. Or, I do the bare minimum to progress. Sure, I have all the options in the world to build and decorate a house and make it my own, but… that feels like a lot of work. And I am not an artist.

It has been revealed that the “cozy” elements of Grand Theft Auto VI are admittedly different from those in a game like Pokopia or Animal Crossing. You’re not designing your home (though you can pick a paint color), but it feels similar, and I am trying to figure out why I enjoy it here as opposed to other games. Is it because Jason and Lucia are so instantly believable as human beings that I want their home to be nicer?

After some thought, I think it might just come down to Grand Theft Auto VI’s consistently impressive visual fidelity. Replacing the shingles on the roof, for example, offers a close-up look at Jason’s character model, and you can practically feel the texture of the asphalt while the heat of the sun beats down.

I don’t have confirmation, but it also just feels like someone at Rockstar did exhaustive research on what the process of replacing a roof shingle should look like, even if, I’m sure, it probably doesn’t quite work that way in the real world. Jason makes it look incredibly easy, to the point that it had me questioning if I should be climbing up to my own roof and taking care of some loose shingles myself. And you know what is a lot of fun? Watching someone who is good at something do the thing they’re good at.

I’m now into the driving and shooting part of the game (and enjoying that, too!), but I am shocked at how grateful I was to have the option to stay home and put up drywall.

Gadgets ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Lifehacker ↗ Open Full Page

10 Movies Like ‘Interstellar’ You Should Watch Next

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1274 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, christopher Nolan’s 2014 megahit Interstellar has it all: substantial sci-fi ideas, cool robots, ugly crying, and a Matt Damon character in need of rescuing.
  • If you loved both the special effects in Interstellar that make space travel feel viscerally thrilling (and terrifying) and the mind-blowing concepts, this is the film for you.
  • Sources indicate that if you’re looking for more existential missions with somewhat reluctant heroes in space, Project Hail Mary is your next stop.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, christopher Nolan’s 2014 megahit Interstellar has it all: substantial sci-fi ideas, cool robots, ugly crying, and a Matt Damon character in need of rescuing. Grounded in the intensity of the human experience, this story of humanity’s potential extinction and the sacrifice of one man to save it doesn’t just deliver exotic planets and thrilling spaceship maneuvers; it also provides all the feels as Joseph Cooper (Matthew McConaughey) sacrifices everything he has in an effort to save the entire human race. It’s one of the best science fiction films ever made, with Nolan’s signature complexity, time manipulations, and emotional wallop. If you love this movie, here are ten more that offer a similar viewing experience.

If you loved both the special effects in Interstellar that make space travel feel viscerally thrilling (and terrifying) and the mind-blowing concepts, this is the film for you. Stanley Kubrick’s 1968 epic (written by sci-fi master Arthur C. Clarke) traces humanity’s development from mildly smart apes to spacefaring capitalists who discover a mysterious obelisk on the Moon that sparks a mission to Jupiter. While it operates in a colder emotional key than Nolan’s film, 2001: A Space Odyssey absolutely delivers on the epic side of things (and the cool—if slightly deranged and deadly—artificial intelligences). Stream 2001: A Space Odyssey on HBO Max or rent it on Prime Video.

Sources indicate that if you’re looking for more existential missions with somewhat reluctant heroes in space, Project Hail Mary is your next stop. When the Sun begins to dim due to the interference of an alien entity, scientists identify the one nearby star that isn’t being similarly affected. Brilliant molecular biologist Ryland Grace (Ryan Gosling) winds up forced to go on what is assumed to be a fatal, one-way mission into deep space to try to find a way to save humanity, unexpectedly assisted by a charming alien he names Rocky. It’s got the same emotional volume and big ideas as Interstellar, and fans of Nolan’s film will love it. Stream Project Hail Mary on MGM+ or Philo, or rent it on Prime Video.

Industry observers note that part of what makes Interstellar so compelling is the stakes: The human race is slowly dying, and a handful of people must make incredible sacrifices to save it. That’s the vibe of Sunshine, set in a future where the Sun is dimming and a spacecraft is dispatched to deliver an enormous bomb designed to reignite the Sun’s fusion cycle. But the mission is the second attempt after the first ship vanished mysteriously seven years earlier, and when the latest crew stumbles on the derelict wreck of the first mission, things rapidly descend into violence and madness—but the crew remains determined to save the world, no matter the cost. Rent Sunshine on Prime Video.

Interstellar works in large part because of the emotional dynamics at play. McConaughey’s character leaves his children behind and is forced to witness them growing up without him, missing out on their lives and saddled with the knowledge that they resent him despite the necessity of his mission. Arrival is a First Contact story focused on language—linguist Louise Banks (Amy Adams) is drafted into an effort to understand the strange, complex language of the aliens. As she slowly builds to an understanding of how the aliens communicate and perceive time itself, her own heartbreak and loss come into play, giving this film a similarly devastating emotional punch. Stream Arrival on Kanopy or Hoopla, or rent it on Prime Video.

Recent findings suggest that family dynamics and the toll of lonely space missions fuel Ad Astra, a film with the same emotional core as Interstellar. Twenty-nine years ago, famed astronaut Clifford McBride (Tommy Lee Jones) led the Lima Project, a space station around Neptune searching for intelligent life. Thirteen years ago, Earth lost contact with him. When bursts of energy emanating from Neptune threaten to end life on Earth, his son, Roy (Brad Pitt), is dispatched to try to make contact with his father. It’s an epic journey with a powerful climax that will satisfy fans of Interstellar in every way. Stream Ad Astra on Netflix or rent it on Prime Video.

Ridley Scott’s prequel to Alien has its flaws, but if you’re looking for a sense of epic spacefaring adventure in the same key as Interstellar, it’s perfect. When two scientists discover a star map apparently left behind by ancient aliens, they secure funding from the Wayland Corporation to organize a space expedition to the indicated planet. Accompanied by a colorful crew and the android David, they discover an apparently abandoned outpost of the species dubbed the Engineers. The story wrestles with questions about humanity’s origins, purpose, and potential—but this being an Alien film, things swiftly turn horrifying. Rent Prometheus on Prime Video.

In a recent development, adapted from Carl Sagan’s 1985 novel, Contact follows astronomer Dr. Ellie Arroway (Jodie Foster), who becomes involved with an effort to decipher a signal originating from the star Vega. The signal turns out to be a set of instructions for constructing a one-person spacecraft of some kind, and Arroway is eventually selected as the candidate to take the journey. There’s a sense of courage in the face of the unknown that’s similar to Interstellar, as well as the thrill of strapping into a spaceship and pressing the ignition. Plus, there’s the added bonus of seeing one of the greatest trick shots in cinematic history. Rent Contact on Prime Video.

Stanislaw Lem’s 1961 novel Solaris explores what Lem saw as the impossibility of ever understanding a truly alien life. The two major adaptations—Andrei Tarkovsky's 1972 version and Steven Soderbergh’s 2002 take starring George Clooney—are both worth watching, but Tarkovsky’s film is a masterpiece of psychological horror. The story is set mainly aboard a space station orbiting a planet covered in what appears to be a sentient "ocean" and chronicles the strange haunting and inexplicable experiences of the humans living on the station. If your favorite part of Interstellar is the ending when things get trippy and weird, you’ll probably love Solaris. Stream Solaris on HBO Max, Plex, or Tubi, or rent it on Prime Video.

In a recent development, the story of a mission to Jupiter’s moon Europa to search for intelligent life, Europa Report has the same sense of terrifying excitement that accompanies Interstellar’s missions to the different candidate planets. Leaning into the fragility of life in an environment not designed to support it, the mission crew face a steady stream of loss and danger as they work to catch sight of alien life on the frozen, deadly moon, ultimately faced with making terrifying sacrifices in order to provide humanity with the answers that it seeks. Stream Europa Report on Netflix, Kanopy, or Hoopla, or rent it on Prime Video.

A film based on a 1956 epic science fiction poem written by a Swedish Nobel Laureate might seem like an unlikely match for fans of Interstellar, but it’s actually perfect. As the Earth becomes uninhabitable, humanity begins launching ships to colonize Mars. When one such ship, the Aniara, is damaged and veers irreversibly off course, the passengers and crew are faced with the knowledge that they will sail off into the void without hope of rescue. Within a few years, despair has driven some to suicide and madness, while others cling to the possibility that they might yet find a way back. The film offers a different perspective on the existential crisis of humanity’s extinction, exploring the worst-case scenario to its bitter, bleak end. Stream Aniara on Kanopy or Hoopla, or rent it on Prime Video.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A newly introduced Honkai: Star Rail Special Program has concluded, which means some fresh news about the game’s upcoming major revision. Version 4.1, unveiled today as Unraveled for Daybreak, is the action RPG’s next moment, kicking off on March 25.

In a recent development, unraveled for Daybreak is the next chapter in the ongoing story of Planarcadia, with the Astra Express Crew now invited to a fan fest inspired by their own past journeys. The aptly named Star Rail Fest is ostensibly hosted to allow more of the citizens of Arcadia to experience the Trailblaze.

As everyone’s eyes is fixated on the grand Star Rail Fest, the Phantasmoon Games continue to be in full swing, as does the war with the Supplicants. Star Rail Fest is, however, the big focus of this revision, in case it wasn't obvious.

The event is made up of three large-scale zones, each themed around past excursions of the Astral Express. You’ll get to explore the Belobog Zone, Xianzhou Luofu Zone, and Penacony Zone. Later on, you’ll also be able to visit Pearluxe Tower, the headquarters of Pearluxe Corp.

Each area will feature its own attractions, such as the balloon figures of Supreme Guardian Cocolia and the Destruction Engine, the duel against the Lord Ravager Phantylia at Scalegorge Waterscape, and the Pearluxe Tower’s Alloy King Pom-Pom model.

The hot upcoming arrival is bumbling noirish detective Ashveil whom we've met in Version 4.0, and who becomes a playable character with this update. Ashveil is a 5-Star Lightning-Type character, on the Path of The Hunt. You’ll be able to pull for him throughout 4.1's runtime, which is slightly reduced at four weeks instead of the usual six, in order to rebalance the schedule after the extra-long Version 3.8.

In combat, Ashveil is capable of increasing Crit Damage of all allies. He can also mark an enemy as Bait, which reduces the Defence of all enemies on the field so long as this tag holds. If Ashveil uses his Skill on the baited target, he will deal extra Damage and regain Skill Points for the team.

In a recent development, ashveil can bully that baited target even further by launching Hounding Pursuit. If any of his teammates attacks the Bait, he can further deliver a follow-up attack that gradually accumulates Gluttony for as long as he’s in combat. Gluttony can later be consumed to boost follow-up attack damage.

Industry observers note that if he lands a kill, Ashveil continues to deal damage to the next enemy he attacks. That buff is transferred if that enemy is killed. Even in map exploration, Ashveil can be deadly, capable of inflicting Stunned upon enemies within a specific range.

Returning characters this patch will be Hyacine in the first half, and Boothill in the second half. Once again, due to the reduced runtime, their banner reruns will be slightly shorter than normal, at just two weeks each instead of three — so be sure to take that into account if you're planning on pulling for either of them.

Version 4.1 also adds the Wispae War Saga, a latest activity where you can practice your leadership skills by commanding different types of Wispae Soldiers in the Graphia Academy. You can upgrade each one, use spell cards to alter their effects, and later face other champions. You ultimately want to play this to unlock new Wispae Companions, not to mention complete the challenges within.
